known_facts_book1: Is fighting the Unicorn for the crown when Alice arrives, in such a cloud of dust that she cannot tell which is which.
Is the subject of the old song in which the Lion beat the Unicorn all round the town and both were drummed out of town.
Looks very tired and sleepy with his eyes half shut, and speaks in a deep hollow tone like the tolling of a great bell.
Asks Alice whether she is animal, vegetable or mineral, yawning at every other word.
Calls Alice 'the Monster' and tells her to hand round the plum-cake and to sit down for fair play with the cake.
Claims he would win easily, and reminds the Unicorn he beat him all round the town, calling him a chicken.
Says there was too much dust to see anything, so he does not know which way round the town they went.
Rises to his feet with the Unicorn, angry at being interrupted in the feast, when the drums begin.

known_relations_book1.Unicorn: His opponent in the fight for the crown, each of them down about eighty-seven times.
known_relations_book1.White King: The King whose crown they are fighting for, who calls the ten minutes for refreshments.
known_relations_book1.Alice: The 'Monster' he asks to carve and hand round the plum-cake.

not_in_this_book: the Lion is king of the Looking-glass world

known_facts_book1: Is distinguished from the Lion by his horn, and ran the Lion through with it during the fight.
Saunters by with his hands in his pockets and asks the King whether he had the best of it this time.
Looks at Alice with the deepest disgust and asks 'What—is—this?', having always thought children were fabulous monsters.
Strikes a bargain with Alice: if she will believe in him, he will believe in her.
Demands the plum-cake and refuses the brown bread.
Explains that Looking-glass cake has to be handed round first and cut afterwards.
Complains that the Monster has given the Lion twice as much cake as him.

known_relations_book1.Lion: His opponent in the fight for the crown, whom he claims he is not sure of losing to.
known_relations_book1.Alice: The 'fabulous monster' he agrees to believe in if she believes in him.
known_relations_book1.White King: Addressed as 'old man' when the Unicorn calls for the plum-cake.

known_facts_book1: Is one of the White King's two Messengers, pronounced by the King so as to rhyme with 'mayor'.
Comes along the road skipping up and down and wriggling like an eel, with his great hands spread out like fans — the King calls these Anglo-Saxon attitudes.
Lives on the Hill, according to the King, in answer to Alice's alphabet game.
Carries a bag round his neck holding ham sandwiches, hay and a large plum-cake, and feeds the fainting King from it.
Reports that he passed Nobody on the road.
Puts his arm affectionately round Hatta's neck and asks him whether he was happy in prison.
Introduces Alice to the Unicorn as a child they only found to-day, as large as life and twice as natural, and says solemnly that it can talk.

known_relations_book1.White King: His master, one of the two Messengers kept so that one comes and one goes.
known_relations_book1.Hatta: The other Messenger, whom he greets as 'dear child' when he comes out of prison.
known_relations_book1.Alice: Introduces her to the Unicorn and hands her the plum-cake to hold.

known_facts_book1: Is the White King's other Messenger, watching the fight with a cup of tea in one hand and bread-and-butter in the other.
Is only just out of prison, where they gave them nothing but oyster-shells, and had not finished his tea when he was sent in.
Weeps when asked whether he was happy in prison and will not say a word about it.
Reports that the Lion and the Unicorn have each been down about eighty-seven times.
Is threatened with buttering by the King for shouting instead of whispering.
Goes bounding away like a grasshopper to order the drums to begin.

known_relations_book1.White King: His master, who threatens to have him buttered and sends him to order the drums.
known_relations_book1.Haigha: The other Messenger, who greets him fondly outside the prison.
known_relations_book1.Alice: Present at the fight beside her; they never speak to each other directly.

not_in_this_book: Hatta wears a top hat marked 10/6
Hatta was tried by the King of Hearts
